length.text: Small and slender; the longest measured was 66 cm

reproduction.text: Lays eggs (kept inside the body for a long time before laying)

overview.text: The Smooth Green Snake is a small, gentle, non-venomous snake of Canada and the northern United States. It is bright green on top, which hides it perfectly in grass.

identification.text: Plain light green on the back with a yellow or white belly. Its back scales are smooth - the Rough Green Snake looks similar but has ridged (keeled) scales.

size.label: Adults
size.text: A slender snake; the longest one measured was 66 cm. The tail is a quarter to half of its length, longer in males.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Southern Canada and scattered parts of the northern and central United States, with small isolated populations further south and west, and in Chihuahua, Mexico.

habitat.text: Marshes, meadows, open woods and the edges of streams.

behaviour.text: Hawks, herons, bears, raccoons, foxes and pet cats all hunt it. People sometimes collect it as a pet, but it does not survive well in captivity.

reproduction.text: Usually lays eggs, but females keep them inside their bodies for a long time first - up to about a month - so the young are already well grown when the eggs are laid.
